page_title: Hourmint: Free Mac Time Tracker with Timesheets and Invoices

sources.entry: Hourmint - Menu bar time tracker for freelancers with a work log, timesheets and PDF invoices. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/abdurrahmanriyad/hourmint) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Hourmint
summary.one_liner: Hourmint is a free, open source macOS menu bar time tracker for freelancers that logs client work and turns it into PDF invoices with attached timesheets.
use_cases: Track billable hours for freelance client work on a Mac
Generate a PDF invoice with an attached timesheet
Log time manually for forgotten timers
Keep an offline record of client hours without a cloud account
Back up and move time tracking data to a new Mac
summary.what_it_does: Hourmint lives in the macOS menu bar, where a timer runs per client and project while you work, with recent tasks available for quick restart. Entries are labelled Timer, Manual or Edited, and billed hours are locked so they cannot be changed or billed twice. Users can review time by day, week or custom range, and mark time as non-billable. To invoice, users pick a client and period, untick unwanted hours, and Hourmint builds a PDF invoice with the timesheet attached, supporting rounding, tax, discounts, per-client currency and rates, and custom invoice numbering. Data stays in a local database file, with no account, analytics or sync.
notable: Open source under the MIT licence, with no premium tier, trial or ads
Timesheet entries labelled Timer, Manual or Edited, and billed hours locked
Local-first: no account, sync or server; data kept in a single database file
Invoices built from unbilled hours with rounding, tax, discounts and custom numbering
caveats: Mac only; no Windows or Linux version yet
No sync between Macs and no phone app; moving data requires manual backup and restore
Not notarized by Apple, so macOS asks for confirmation on first launch
Does not send invoices to clients; the user sends the PDF themselves
